definitions.explanation: Cured, usually smoked pork belly, sold in thin slices or thick blocks. In Japan it is most often eaten in breakfast dishes, pasta, and stir-fries rather than as a standalone side.

examples.japanese: ベーコン⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{焼|や}いた→焼く：01123_yaku⟧。
⟦{朝食|ちょうしょく}→朝食：03122_choushoku⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧ベーコンエッグにした。
examples.english: I had bacon and eggs for breakfast.

examples.japanese: ベーコン⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{細|こま}かく→細かい：01245_komakai⟧⟦{切|き}って→切る：02693_kiru⟧、⟦{野菜|やさい}→野菜：02265_yasai⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{一緒|いっしょ}→一緒：02848_issho⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{炒|いた}めて→炒める：01879_itameru⟧⟦ください→ください：02899_kudasai⟧。
examples.english: Please chop the bacon finely and stir-fry it together with the vegetables.

notes:
A loanword from English "bacon". Supermarket packs are usually thin slices (スライスベーコン); thick-cut blocks are sold as ⟦ブロック→ブロック：05902_burokku⟧ベーコン and cut into batons for cooking.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ベーコンエッグ: bacon and eggs
- ベーコン⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{炒|いた}める→炒める：01879_itameru⟧: to stir-fry bacon
- ⟦{厚切|あつぎ}り→厚切り：07476_atsugiri⟧ベーコン: thick-cut bacon
- ベーコン{巻|ま}き: something wrapped in bacon

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦ハム→ハム：09755_hamu⟧: ham — cured but typically not smoked, eaten cold
- ⟦{豚|ぶた}→豚：04710_buta⟧バラ{肉|にく}: pork belly — the uncured cut bacon is made from
